title: Veteran-focused SNAP outreach can reach a recommendation and coordination stage while benefit access and food security remain open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108111 review of SNAP outreach to veterans
geography: United States veterans and veteran households eligible for or receiving SNAP through state-administered outreach

observations.period: 2015–2020 food-insecurity estimate, fiscal year 2026 state outreach plans, and October 1, 2026 GAO review

denominator.unit: states with fiscal year 2026 SNAP outreach plans reviewed for whether veterans were identified as a target group

food_insecurity_exposure.unit: average annual number of veterans estimated by a 2023 RAND report to have faced food insecurity from 2015 through 2020

state_outreach_targeting.unit: states among 47 with fiscal year 2026 outreach plans that identified veterans as a target group

coordination_status.value: VA and USDA established a memorandum of agreement in September 2023, but officials told GAO collaboration slowed after April 2025 and the agreement had not been reviewed as specified, leaving its current status unclear

recommendation_status.unit: open GAO recommendations to USDA and VA concerning current eligibility information, veteran-tailored outreach materials, and a formal collaboration mechanism

access_conversion.unit: veteran contact, application, eligibility, approval, benefit receipt, benefit adequacy, food security, household recovery, trust, or durable participation

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108111, including its review of state outreach plans, agency documentation, Census analysis, interviews, and open recommendations. Exposure, outreach targeting, coordination, recommendations, and benefit outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The food-insecurity estimate is a secondary 2015–2020 estimate and is not a current SNAP-eligible denominator. State plan targeting indicates intended outreach, not completed contact or receipt. The report does not measure veteran-level application, approval, payment, adequacy, or food-security conversion.
observations.subgroup: Veterans and veteran households with limited or uncertain food access, including people reached through VA, state SNAP agencies, and veteran organizations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower veteran SNAP participation may reflect eligibility, income, administrative burden, stigma, beliefs, or alternative supports rather than outreach alone; tailored materials and interagency coordination can improve information without guaranteeing benefit access or adequate food.

related_sources.claim: The official GAO report PDF contains the veteran food-insecurity, outreach-plan, coordination, and recommendation findings.
The GAO companion explanation describes veteran SNAP participation barriers and outreach context.

boundary: This record advances a bounded veteran food-insecurity-to-outreach-and-interagency-recommendation route. It does not establish veteran-level eligibility, application, approval, benefit receipt, adequacy, food security, household recovery, trust, or completed agency action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; official report PDF and companion explanation are retained for reproduction.
